summary: Hamilton County, NY fire-watch tower built in 1916 on T-Lake Mountain; closed after the 1970 season and brought down by Army engineers in 1977. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Brought down by Army engineers' explosive test in 1977; remains removed by helicopter. No source describes the site today.
facts.agency: New York State Conservation Commission (1916); the state Conservation Department by 1928

events.note: Conservation Commission built a 50-foot Aermotor LL25 tower on the mountain
New mountain station in operation for part of the season, per the state's 6th Annual Report as quoted on Forest Lookouts
Wooden steps added inside the tower in 1918 or 1919
New observer's cabin built, one of several that year
Observer Emerson Nye resigned after about ten years; the article gives his age as 78
Self-supporting staircase, a tower within a tower, replaced the wooden steps
Fire watching ceased at the end of the 1970 season because aerial detection had made lookouts less necessary
Army engineers tested shaped explosive charges on the tower, which brought it down
Remains removed by helicopter a few weeks after the explosive test

notes_for_editor: Gone since 1977; no source describes the site today, so the story says so and gives no view or remains. Height conflicts (50 ft per Wikipedia vs one hundred feet in the 1924 newspaper quoted on Forest Lookouts); height_m left out. Wikipedia summit elevation (3,058 ft) differs from figures in other sites; not used. Wikipedia's own references were not checked, so its 1977 account rests on a secondary source; the Forest Lookouts newspaper quotes were read on the cached page. Access not stated by any source read, so facts.access is omitted. Budget: 1 WebSearch, 7 page reads (one more than the 6 allowed, because the 1928 article sat in the Forest Lookouts page and needed a second grep). No photos found.
